cases.reason: feOffset moves SourceGraphic by dx, dy in user units.
With primitiveUnits=objectBoundingBox, dx and dy are fractions of the bounding box.
The filter region is a hard clip on the filter result.
The default filter region is -10%, -10%, 120%, 120% of the bounding box.
filterUnits=objectBoundingBox resolves x, y, width and height against the bounding box.
feFlood fills its subregion, by default the filter region, with flood-color.
x, y, width and height of a primitive set its subregion in primitiveUnits.
Subregion attributes in objectBoundingBox primitive units are fractions or percentages of the box.
A subregion is clipped by the filter region.
A primitive with a zero-width subregion is disabled: its result is transparent black.
flood-opacity multiplies the flood color's alpha.
A transparent flood-color stays transparent whatever flood-opacity is.
feMerge composites its nodes in order, each over the previous ones.
Later feMergeNode inputs are drawn over earlier ones.
SourceAlpha is the source's alpha with black color.
in names the closest preceding primitive with that result.
When a result name repeats, references use the closest preceding primitive.
A reference to a non-existent result acts as unspecified: the previous result.
A first primitive without a usable in reads SourceGraphic.
Without x/y/width/height a primitive's subregion is the union of its referenced results' subregions.
Referencing a standard input makes the default subregion the filter region.
operator=in keeps the input where in2 has alpha.
operator=out keeps the input where in2 is transparent.
The initial operator is over, drawing in over in2.
operator=atop draws in over in2 only where in2 has alpha.
operator=xor keeps each input where the other is transparent.
operator=arithmetic computes k1 i1 i2 + k2 i1 + k3 i2 + k4, clamped.
feBlend blends in onto in2 with the mode's blend function, like mix-blend-mode.
type=matrix applies the 5x4 matrix to straight RGBA.
A matrix with the wrong number of values falls back to the identity default.
luminanceToAlpha moves luminance to alpha and zeroes color.
saturate defaults to 1, which leaves colors unchanged.
Each feFuncX maps its channel: linear, table and discrete.
type=gamma computes amplitude C^exponent + offset.
A later feFuncR replaces an earlier one.
dilate takes the maximum over a (2 rx + 1) x (2 ry + 1) window.
erode, the initial operator, takes the minimum; two numbers give x and y radii.
A zero radius disables the primitive: the result is the input.
feTile repeats its input's subregion across its own subregion.
stdDeviation 0 disables the blur: the result is the input.
A negative stdDeviation disables the blur: the result is the input.
feDropShadow is the offset, flood-colored alpha of its input merged under the input.
An element whose filter has no primitives is not rendered.
A reference to a non-existent object ignores the whole filter chain.
A reference to an element that is not a filter ignores the whole filter chain.
One invalid reference ignores every filter in the list.
A zero-width filter region disables rendering of the filtered element.
A filter on an empty group still runs; flood needs no source.
Bounding-box units on an empty bounding box leave nothing to render.
In a filter list each filter's input is the previous filter's result.
The first filter in the list runs first: its region clips before the second filter's offset.
Primitive parameters are in user space and scale with the current transform.
Filters run in the element's local coordinate system and the result is then transformed.
The initial color-interpolation-filters works in linearRGB and converts the result back to sRGB.
An enclosing viewport's clip applies to the filter result.
The filter applies before clip-path, which clips the filtered result.
opacity applies to the filtered result.
A subregion clips the blur's result, not its input: pixels outside it still spread into it.
stdDeviation in objectBoundingBox units scales by the box's width and height.
feDropShadow equals its spec expansion: blur, offset, flood, composite in, merge.
grayscale() is its feColorMatrix equivalent.
sepia() is its feColorMatrix equivalent.
saturate() is feColorMatrix type=saturate.
hue-rotate() is feColorMatrix type=hueRotate in degrees.
invert() is its feComponentTransfer table equivalent.
opacity() scales alpha through a table.
brightness() is a linear transfer with the amount as slope.
contrast() is a linear transfer around 0.5.
blur() is feGaussianBlur with the length as standard deviation, in a region covering its spread.
drop-shadow() is the shadow expansion with its third length as standard deviation.
Filter functions run in sRGB whatever color-interpolation-filters says.
References and functions chain in list order.
A missing reference anywhere in the list ignores every function too.
A filter without primitives uses its href template's primitives and attributes.
Own primitives win; unspecified attributes come from the template.
Templates inherit indirectly through further href references.
A self-referencing href is invalid and ignored.
filterRes matching device pixels reproduces the automatic result.
filterRes sets the intermediate pixel grid (non-integers truncate); a flood stays uniform.
A zero filterRes disables rendering of the filtered element.
A negative filterRes is an error and leaves the automatic resolution.
feTurbulence follows the normative reference code, sampled per pixel in user space.
fractalNoise maps (sum + 1) / 2; stitchTiles adjusts frequencies to the subregion; the seed truncates toward zero.
Noise is defined in user space: a scaled element samples it at device pixels mapped back to user space.
With primitiveUnits=objectBoundingBox the noise lives in bounding box units: baseFrequency is per box width and height.
The seed is truncated toward zero before setup_seed.
Zero frequency samples lattice points, where noise is 0: fractalNoise gives (0 + 1) / 2 in every channel.
Negative base frequencies are unsupported: no noise, transparent black.
A kernel with 1 at the target reproduces the input.
The kernel is applied rotated by 180 degrees: its first entry weighs the pixel down and right of the target.
A kernel whose length is not orderX * orderY makes the primitive a pass through filter.
Orders must be integers greater than zero; otherwise the primitive passes its input through.
Non-integer orders truncate toward zero.
A target outside the kernel is an unfulfilled precondition: pass through.
targetX positions the kernel relative to the target pixel.
A zero kernel sum leaves divisor 1; bias is added to every premultiplied component.
The weighted sum is divided by divisor.
A zero divisor falls back to the kernel sum.
preserveAlpha convolves unpremultiplied color and keeps the source alpha.
edgeMode=wrap extends the input with its opposite edge.
edgeMode defaults to duplicate, which repeats the edge pixels.
P'(x, y) = P(x + scale (A - 0.5), y + scale (A - 0.5)) with the alpha channel by default.
xChannelSelector and yChannelSelector pick the map channels for each axis.
A zero scale leaves the input unchanged.
scale is in primitiveUnits: fractions of the bounding box width along x and height along y.
The displacement scales with the user space.
A flat surface lit from straight above reflects kd * lighting-color, opaque.
Light at zero elevation is perpendicular to a flat surface's normal: N.L = 0 gives opaque black.
diffuseConstant scales the reflected light.
Specular light on a flat surface from straight above: N.H = 1, and alpha is the largest component.
Sa = max(Sr, Sg, Sb) makes the specular result a premultiplied color: half-strength white light is white at half opacity.
Without a light source element there is no light: transparent black.
lighting-color is converted into the primitive's color space like flood-color.
Light positions are in primitiveUnits; z of a bounding box scales by its normalized diagonal.
feSpotLight positions and target are in primitiveUnits; the cone angle's sign does not matter.
Light positions follow the user space transform, z scaling with it.
A PNG feImage renders like image: xMidYMid meet inside the subregion.
preserveAspectRatio="none" stretches the image over the subregion.
xMinYMin slice covers the subregion; the overflow is cut at the subregion.
x, y, width and height place the image in a primitive subregion.
An SVG document reference renders like image, fitted with its intrinsic ratio.
An element reference renders like use in user space; the subregion x/y does not translate it (Chrome does).
With primitiveUnits="objectBoundingBox" the referenced element is drawn in bounding box units.
feImage results feed later primitives by name.
A missing reference fills the subregion with transparent black.
A reference back to the filtered element is a cycle and draws nothing (Chrome draws the element unfiltered).
BackgroundImage is the backdrop under the filter region; feOffset moves it.
BackgroundAlpha keeps only the backdrop alpha, with black color.
The backdrop is that of the current isolation group, empty at the start of an isolated group.
The filter region clips the backdrop like any input (#FilterEffectsRegion), so content left of it does not move in.
FillPaint is the fill with its fill-opacity over the whole filter region (the FE1 subregion example reads it so).
StrokePaint is the stroke paint with its stroke-opacity over the filter region.
A FillPaint paint server keeps the filtered element's bounding box, padded past it.
fill="none" makes FillPaint transparent black.
On a group, FillPaint is the group's own fill, not its children's.
enable-background: new (FE1 Appendix A, SVG 1.1) restarts BackgroundImage: the blue rect drawn before it is not part of it.
An enable-background: new region limits BackgroundImage to that rectangle in the element's user space.
The filtered element's own opacity group applies after the filter, so BackgroundImage is its parent's backdrop.
With no-composite, normal blending yields the source alone: the yellow backdrop is not composited in.
Multiply of blue on yellow is black where the source is; outside it the result keeps the source alpha, 0.
The mixing formula keeps the source alpha: a half-transparent source stays half transparent over an opaque backdrop.
With kernelUnitLength="2" the kernel steps by two user units: the image is resampled to one pixel per unit, convolved and resampled back (bilinearly).
A kernel unit of one device pixel is the default stepping.
A negative or zero kernelUnitLength uses the default.
Lighting with a kernel unit of one device pixel matches the default normals.
A user-space filter region does not depend on content: an empty group still renders its flood.
The SourceGraphic of a group whose only child is empty is transparent black over the whole region.
objectBoundingBox filter units on an empty bounding box disable the filter, so the element is not rendered.
objectBoundingBox primitive units on an empty bounding box also cannot be resolved; the element is not rendered.
A practically infinite filter region is clipped to the canvas and floods all of it.
Huge bounding-box fractions behave like an infinite region and flood the canvas.
feFlood currentColor uses the primitive's computed color, inherited through filter and defs, not the filtered element's.
lighting-color currentColor resolves to the computed color; a flat opaque surface lit from straight above reflects the full light colour.
drop-shadow() currentColor is the filtered element's computed color.
A kernelMatrix whose entries sum to zero uses divisor 1, even when the float sum of its decimals rounds away from zero.
Presentation attributes admit unitless lengths and angles throughout the property grammar, including inside filter functions.
A filter region on a viewport element is in that element's user space, outside its viewBox transform: the bounding box is measured there and the region stays where it was measured.
